    OPT   Est. Speedup: 41%                                                                                             
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 35.5 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 41.0% of the total average of 86.7 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 36.88%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 32.0 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency   
          on a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited  
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 36.9% of the total average of 86.7 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 41.35%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 35.9 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 41.4% of the total average of 86.8 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 39.21%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 34.0 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency   
          on a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited  
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 39.2% of the total average of 86.8 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 47.83%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 32.6 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 47.8% of the total average of 68.2 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 40.11%

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 47.2%                                                                                           
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 41.7 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 47.2% of the total average of 88.4 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 40.04%

          on a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited  
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 40.0% of the total average of 88.4 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 45.6% of the total average of 78.3 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 33.89%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 26.5 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency   
          on a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited  
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 33.9% of the total average of 78.3 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 54.55%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 36.7 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 54.6% of the total average of 67.3 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 40.74%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 27.4 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency   
          on a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited  
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 40.7% of the total average of 67.3 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 42.08%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 43.9 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 42.1% of the total average of 104.3 cycles between issuing two instructions.      
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 35.42%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 36.9 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency   
          on a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited  
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 35.4% of the total average of 104.3 cycles       
          between issuing two instructions.

          On average, each warp of this workload spends 37.0 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency   
          on a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited  
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 42.4% of the total average of 87.3 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.                                                                             
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 41.68%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 36.4 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 41.7% of the total average of 87.3 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

          on each stall reason.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 47.83%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 32.6 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 47.8% of the total average of 68.1 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 40.23%

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 48.61%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 41.7 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 48.6% of the total average of 85.8 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 41.29%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 35.4 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency   
          on a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited  
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 41.3% of the total average of 85.8 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 45.6% of the total average of 78.1 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by

          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 46.9% of the total average of 88.7 cycles between issuing two instructions.
